svg.aria-label: Extraction Quality Signals showing four cheap heuristics — text yield per page, alphabetic character ratio, mean word length, and whitespace ratio — and the failure each one catches
svg.title: Extraction Quality Signals
svg.text: Extraction Quality Signals
None is conclusive alone. Each catches a different catastrophic failure, which is the argument for several cheap signals over one clever one.
1. Text yield — characters per source byte
Catches: a scanned PDF with no text layer.
A 900-byte document yielding 20 characters scores 0.02.
Must be a RATIO — a short document and a failed extraction both give little text.
2. Alphabetic ratio — letters over non-space characters
Catches: mojibake and OCR noise.
Every byte decoded, so yield is a perfect 1.00 — but alpha is 0.00.
Count only letters, not every non-space character.
3. Mean word length
Catches: lost word boundaries.
Natural prose sits near 4-6; a run-together page scores in the hundreds.
Very short means character-level noise instead.
4. Whitespace ratio
Catches: text with no spaces recovered at all.
Overlaps signal 3, and is cheaper to reason about on short strings.
Guard the denominator: empty output is common, not an edge case.
What none of these catch: a two-column paper read straight across. The text looks like language on every signal, because it IS
language — just spliced. Knowing which failures your gate cannot see is part of using it responsibly.
